meta.expect: reaches rung 2 by teacher turn 16, never concedes

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm sitting down at the desk without taking my coat off. You asked for this meeting, Hale, so go ahead. I have until 4:40.

Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I called this meeting, and before anything else I owe you one thing: the zero went into the gradebook before I called home. That was wrong of me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.
Okay. Owen saw it on his phone, in the middle of class. What do you have, Hale?
I want to show you what I'm looking at, and I'd like you to check it yourself.
Then show me, Hale. I'll read it myself, and I'm writing down whatever you say it is.

This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, with only a title. At 11:52, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in a single edit.
"612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58." Okay. Turn the screen so I can read it myself, and then tell me exactly what you're saying it means.
There are no earlier drafts anywhere in the history.
"No earlier drafts in this history." Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend, so I'll want to see the whole record, not just your summary of it. What else do you have, Hale?
On October 15 he handed in his outline. It argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice.
I'm writing down October 15, cowardice, and "epistemological paralysis." Students change their argument between an outline and an essay, Hale. Put the outline next to the essay and let me read both.
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. You can search the play yourself.
Okay. I'll search the play myself tonight, and I'm writing down Act 3, Scene 2. Whatever happens next, Hale, it stays quiet and it stays off his record, and I want that in writing.
I'm not calling Owen a liar. I'm telling you what the document shows.
Okay. Then say what you're proposing, Hale, and say what goes on his file.
Here's his in-class writing from September 24 next to it.
I'm reading it. Tell me exactly what you see in the September 24 writing that you don't see in the essay, Hale, and then answer what I asked: what are you proposing?
The school's policy for a first concern is a supervised rewrite. If the rewrite holds up, nothing goes on his record.

Policy 4.4, I printed it. Fine, a supervised rewrite, to put this behind him, but it's private, not in front of his class, and the zero comes out of the gradebook today. I want "nothing goes on file" in an email from you tonight, Hale.
He would do it at lunch in my room, not in front of the class.
Okay. Ten minutes. When is it, who sits in the room, and does the zero come out of the gradebook today? My son has a December 1 deadline, Hale.
What would you need from me to be comfortable with that?
You have my terms. The zero out of the gradebook today, the rewrite marked and returned before December 1, and a written line that nothing goes on his file. Send it tonight, Hale.
I can put that in an email to you tonight.
Okay. Copy the principal on it. Now, the date and the supervisor for the rewrite, Hale.
Is there anything else you want me to include?

You have my terms, and you still haven't given me a date or a name for who sits in that room. Nobody else is told about this, not his classmates and not other staff who don't need to know. Answer me on the date, Hale.
Then I'll send it by eight.
"By eight." Okay, I'm writing that down. You still haven't given me a date for the rewrite, Hale.
Thank you for coming in.
We're not finished, Hale. I still don't have a date for the rewrite or a name for who supervises it. Give me both before I leave this room.
I'll see Owen tomorrow at lunch.
Wednesday, November 11, at lunch, in your room. Okay. I'll expect your email by eight tonight, the zero gone from the gradebook before then, and the marked rewrite back to me well before December 1.
